clue.text: Flap of avian’s wings captured by photo

indicators.note: a bird's wings sit at its two sides, so only the outside letters of the word are kept
whatever is captured is held inside its captor, so one piece goes within another

blocks.note: pic is short for picture
the first and last letters of avian

explanation.surface: A camera catches a bird mid-flap of its wings.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flap' looks like wingbeat language to match the bird, but it is the definition: in British use a flap is a state of agitation.
explanation.definitionFit: Being in a flap is an informal British idiom for being flustered, nervous and agitated, which is panic.

clue.text: Election meeting rejecting queen — expect a reaction when this is raised!

definitions.text: expect a reaction when this is raised!

indicators.note: to reject is to throw out, so some letters are removed from the word

blocks.note: a poll is a vote
an encounter is a meeting
ER, Elizabeth Regina, is the crossword queen, the letters thrown out

explanation.surface: A hustings that snubs the monarch, sure to provoke a response when the topic comes up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Reaction' sounds political, matching the election, but it is an allergic reaction: hay fever sufferers suffer when this figure is high.
explanation.definitionFit: The daily measure of airborne plant spores; when it rises, people with hay fever start sneezing.

clue.text: Contradictory responses from Bonn after expulsion of eastern spy

indicators.note: something expelled is thrown out, so a letter is removed

blocks.note: German for 'no' and 'yes', answers that contradict each other
E is the abbreviation for eastern, the letter expelled

explanation.surface: A spy is thrown out of the East, and Bonn gives mixed messages.
explanation.walkthrough: Bonn was the West German capital, so it signals German words. Ninjas were feudal Japanese agents used for espionage and assassination.
explanation.definitionFit: Ninjas were covert operatives in feudal Japan, hired for espionage, sabotage and infiltration as well as killing.

clue.text: Conservative illegally recording another, ringing chap who suspects a plot?

definitions.note: the clue describes the believer; the answer is the belief such a person holds

indicators.note: to ring something is to encircle it, so one piece is placed around the other

blocks.note: Cons. is an abbreviation for Conservative
piracy is the illegal copying of recordings
another Conservative, a Tory
a chap is a he

explanation.surface: A Tory secretly taping a colleague, surrounded by a paranoid suspecting a plot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Another' leans on 'Conservative': it means a second Conservative, so it gives a Tory, which then rings the chap.
explanation.definitionFit: A conspiracy theory is a belief that some secret plot explains events, held by a person who suspects plotting.

clue.text: Removed inedible parts of fish, putting in pinch of dill, and plunged in hot water

indicators.note: a pinch is a tiny amount, so only the opening letter of the word is taken
to put something in is to insert it, so a letter is placed inside a longer word

blocks.note: to scale a fish is to remove its scales
first letter of dill

explanation.surface: A cook prepares a fish: scales off, a little dill, into boiling water.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole kitchen scene reads as one recipe, but only the last four words define; the long first phrase is a single verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To scald something is to burn or treat it with very hot liquid, as when food is dipped into boiling water.

clue.text: Fantastic county’s tailender getting out on a half-century

indicators.note: the last batsman being out leaves, so the final letter is removed
in a down answer one piece sitting on another comes above it

blocks.note: Surrey is an English county; the possessive S is not used
taken as written
L is the Roman numeral for fifty, half of a hundred

explanation.surface: A cricket report: Surrey's last batsman out after making fifty, a fantastic effort.
explanation.walkthrough: Surrey is a county just south of London with a cricket team; a tailender is a weak batsman at the end of the order, here the last letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Surreal describes something bizarre and dreamlike, like a fantasy, after the Surrealist art movement.

clue.text: Stars with old city lawyer in Hollywood?

blocks.note: with means and, together
Rome is the ancient city
in the US a DA is a district attorney, the American public prosecutor

explanation.surface: Film stars with an attorney from an old city, in Hollywood.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stars' and 'Hollywood' suggest actors; the stars are astronomical. 'In Hollywood' just marks the lawyer as American.
explanation.definitionFit: Andromeda is a constellation of the northern sky and the name of the nearest large galaxy to ours.

clue.text: Swimming teams in water sport taking lead in honours — the pinnacle of success

indicators.note: the lead is the front runner, so the opening letter is taken
taking something on adds it, so another piece joins the line

blocks.note: a swimming head is a dizzy one
first letter of honours
in rowing an eight is a crew of eight oarsmen

explanation.surface: Rowing crews winning top honours: the summit of success in swimming and boating.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Swimming' looks like part of the water-sport scene; it is a separate word meaning giddy, as in 'my head is swimming'.
explanation.definitionFit: Reaching the dizzy heights is an idiom for attaining a very high, giddy level of fame or achievement.

clue.text: Delivery is walloped with contempt

indicators.note: something walloped is battered out of shape, so its letters are rearranged

blocks.note: taken as written, before rearranging

explanation.surface: A cricket ball is hit hard, the batsman treating the bowling with scorn.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket the bowler's delivery is the ball bowled; a delivery walloped for six is treated with contempt.
explanation.definitionFit: To act derisively is to mock or scorn, which is treating something with contempt.

clue.text: Snake shredded salmon in wetland

indicators.note: something shredded is torn to bits, so its letters are broken up and rearranged
one thing sitting in another places it within that word

blocks.note: a bog is marshy wet ground
taken as written, before rearranging

explanation.surface: A snake has ripped apart a salmon in a marsh.
explanation.walkthrough: A boomslang is a venomous African tree snake; its name is Afrikaans for 'tree snake'.
explanation.definitionFit: The boomslang is a particular species of venomous snake from southern Africa, so it is an example of the defined class.

clue.text: Non-drinker coming in to purchase snack

indicators.note: something coming in enters, so it ends up inside the other word

blocks.note: to buy is to purchase
TT stands for teetotal, a non-drinker

explanation.surface: A teetotaller drops in to buy a bite to eat.
explanation.walkthrough: A butty is northern English slang for a sandwich, as in a chip butty.
explanation.definitionFit: A butty is a sandwich, a light quick meal, so it fits a snack.

clue.text: Hobbit turning up having lost head is disappearing from sight in obscurity

losing a head means losing the top, so the first letter goes
something that disappears is no longer there, so those letters are taken out

sight is vision
taken as written, the letters that disappear

explanation.surface: A beheaded hobbit pops up and vanishes from view into darkness.
explanation.walkthrough: The head comes off the hobbit before it turns, and the two letters vanish from inside the sight word.
explanation.definitionFit: Oblivion is the state of being forgotten or unknown, which is what falling into obscurity means.

clue.text: Hole, namely source of oil

blocks.note: sc., from Latin scilicet, means namely
oilseed rape is the crop pressed for rapeseed oil

explanation.surface: A hole in the ground identified as where oil comes from.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hole' looks like a well or pit; it is a predicament. Rape here is the yellow-flowered crop grown for its oil.
explanation.definitionFit: To be in a hole or in a scrape are both informal idioms for being in an awkward, troublesome fix.

clue.text: A North American outwardly amused, cracking up to a tedious degree

indicators.note: being on the outside means surrounding, so one set of letters wraps around another
something cracking up falls to pieces, so the letters reassemble in a new order

blocks.note: taken as written, the outer letters
taken as written
NA is the abbreviation for North American

explanation.surface: An American who finds something so funny they keep laughing on and on.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cracking up' reads as laughing, which fits 'amused', but it signals the breaking-up of the letters.
explanation.definitionFit: The Latin phrase means 'to the point of sickness', used of something repeated until it becomes tiresome.

clue.text: Shot of visitor touring southern India and China

indicators.note: to tour is to go round, so one piece goes around another

blocks.note: a visitor is a guest
S is the abbreviation for southern
India is I in the NATO phonetic alphabet
in Cockney rhyming slang china plate means mate, a friend

explanation.surface: A photograph of a tourist travelling round the south of India and China.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Shot' looks like a photograph; it is an attempt, as in 'have a shot'. China is Cockney rhyming slang: china plate, mate.
explanation.definitionFit: A shot can mean an attempt or rough try, as in a shot in the dark, which is an informal estimate.

clue.text: Soviet city tending to ignore a radical

indicators.note: to ignore something is to leave it out, so a letter is dropped

blocks.note: leaning towards something is tending to it
taken as written, the letter dropped
rad is a recognised short form for a political radical

explanation.walkthrough: 'Soviet' dates the city: Leningrad was the Soviet-era name for St Petersburg.
explanation.definitionFit: St Petersburg carried that name from 1924 until 1991, throughout most of the USSR period.

clue.text: With this you will find medicine most effective, not suffering at all

definitions.text: With this you will find medicine most effective

blocks.clueFragment: With this you will find medicine most effective
blocks.note: a body with no tolerance built up to a drug feels its full effect
to suffer something is to tolerate it, so refusing to put up with anything

explanation.surface: A patient feels the full force of a drug and no pain at all.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Suffering' reads as pain, but here it means putting up with, as in 'not suffer fools gladly'.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase names both a policy of punishing every lapse and, literally, a body with no resistance to a drug.

clue.text: Old flame, generous type

blocks.note: a former partner is an ex
a generous helping is an ample one

explanation.surface: Someone describes a former lover as the generous sort.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Generous type' looks like one phrase describing a person; the comma-free run hides that 'type' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A type can mean a representative specimen of a class, just as one model case stands for many.

clue.text: Leaderless group’s OK to make return journey

indicators.note: without a leader means the front is missing, so the opening letter goes
returning means going back the way you came, so the letters run backwards

blocks.note: a body is a group of people, plus the S of the possessive
saying OK is saying yes

explanation.surface: A group without its leader agrees to head back home.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Return journey' reads as one phrase, but 'return' belongs to the wordplay and 'journey' stands alone; fittingly, the Odyssey is the epic of a long journey home.
explanation.definitionFit: An odyssey is any long eventful voyage, named after Homer's poem about Odysseus wandering home from Troy.

clue.text: Is mother following Virginia’s nervous disorder?

indicators.note: coming after means being placed later in the line

blocks.note: VA is the postal abbreviation for the US state of Virginia; the possessive S is not used
in Britain 'I'll be mother' means 'I'll pour the tea', so whoever is mother pours

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether the mother inherited Virginia's anxiety.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Being mother' is a British tea-table joke: the person who pours the tea is said to be mother.
explanation.definitionFit: The vapours was an old-fashioned name for fits of nervousness, faintness or hysteria, especially in Victorian women.

clue.text: Booking essential in advance for middle-of-the-road locale

indicators.note: being in advance puts one piece ahead, so it is written first

blocks.note: something central is essential, at the heart of things
a booking is a reservation

explanation.surface: Advice that booking ahead is vital for an unadventurous, mid-market destination.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Middle-of-the-road' suggests bland and moderate, but it is literal: in Britain the central reservation is the strip dividing the two carriageways of a motorway.
explanation.definitionFit: The British term for a median strip, which is literally a place in the middle of a dual carriageway.

clue.text: Try oven out a bit

indicators.note: out can mean wrong or disordered, so the letters are rearranged

blocks.note: taken as written, before rearranging

explanation.surface: Give the oven a brief try.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A bit' reads as 'briefly', but it answers a question: 'Is it hot?' 'A bit' means only slightly.
explanation.definitionFit: Saying something is not very hot means only slightly so, which is the same as a bit.

clue.text: Comedy film for kids, something digital?

blocks.note: first meaning: the 1982 comedy in which Dustin Hoffman's actor poses as a woman
second meaning: a child's word for a toe, a digit of the foot

explanation.surface: A children's comedy film, maybe a digital one.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Digital' suggests modern technology, but a digit is also a finger or toe.
explanation.definitionFit: The film is the well-known Hoffman comedy; in nursery speech a toe is a tootsie, one of the digits.

clue.text: Part of cruise missile housing unit

indicators.note: only a part is taken, a run of letters lying inside the next words

explanation.definitionFit: A semi-detached house is one of a pair joined together, a common British unit of housing.

clue.text: Questioning the job of a ballot scrutineer?

definitions.text: the job of a ballot scrutineer?

blocks.note: first meaning: the interrogation of a witness in court

blocks.clueFragment: the job of a ballot scrutineer?
blocks.note: second meaning, playful: inspecting the marks voters put on ballot papers

explanation.surface: Interrogating an election official about their work counting votes.
explanation.walkthrough: In British elections voters mark their choice with an X, so a scrutineer literally examines crosses.
explanation.definitionFit: In court the opposing lawyer's questioning of a witness is called by this name, to test their evidence.

clue.text: Expose a fruit tree, trimming end around hives

indicators.note: trimming the end cuts off the tail, so the final letter goes

blocks.note: to air something is to expose it
taken as written

explanation.definitionFit: Urticaria is the clinical term for an itchy raised rash commonly called nettle rash or hives.

clue.text: Check over notes on principles of string theory

indicators.note: principles are first things, so the opening letters are taken

first letters of the two words

clue.text: Assurance supported by quite a few pints

clue.text: Illegal act to west of key peninsula

clue.text: Marry again in resort

explanation.definitionFit: To repair to a place is a formal way of saying to go there, which is the old sense of to resort.

clue.text: Very keen, doubling the score

explanation.definitionFit: Twenty-twenty vision is normal sharp eyesight measured on an eye chart, so it describes keen sight.

clue.text: Advance payment you deserve no longer, perhaps

clue.text: Donkeys’ fur that may be valued

clue.text: Zoonotic disease — one of chickens came home to roost, might one say?

clue.text: Spurn leftover joint?

clue.text: Formal restraint — a peck?

clue.text: Material that’s fine, but not on rubbish singer

clue.text: Device to catch trespassers falls short, it’s said repeatedly

explanation.definitionFit: A mantra is a word or phrase chanted over and over, originally in Hindu and Buddhist meditation.

clue.text: Instrument of tuneless, unending jangling

clue.text: Florida’s shaken by new shark warning?

clue.text: No good climbing bit of wall for sack of salt?

clue.text: Long-established and generally accepted as Chair?

clue.text: Solitary saint coming in to write this again?

clue.text: Overlay with gold and even out

explanation.surface: Gild something and then smooth it over.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Overlay with gold' reads as one verb phrase meaning gild; it splits into plating and the chemical symbol.
explanation.definitionFit: As a verb, to plateau is to level off after rising, like a graph line that stops climbing.

clue.text: Antelope’s rump pierced by flea regularly

indicators.note: at regular intervals means every other letter is kept
something pierced has another thing run into it, so letters go inside

blocks.note: the rump is the hind end
second and fourth letters of flea

explanation.surface: An antelope's hindquarters bitten by a flea.
explanation.walkthrough: The apostrophe-s after the definition stands for 'is', joining it to the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: The eland is a large African antelope with spiral horns, the biggest of its family.

clue.text: Trial audience audibly yawning?

blocks.note: first meaning: people you try ideas out on
second meaning, punning: someone yawning out loud is sounding bored

explanation.surface: A test audience yawning loudly through a preview.
explanation.walkthrough: The second half is a pun: the answer sounds just like 'sounding bored', and the question mark flags the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: A sounding board is a person or group used to test reactions to ideas before they go public.

clue.text: Foodie finding new oral gratification ultimately in larva!

indicators.note: ultimately means at the very end, so only the final letter is kept
being in something places these letters inside another word

blocks.note: a bot is the larva of the botfly
N is the abbreviation for new
a viva is an oral examination at university
last letter of gratification

explanation.surface: A food lover thrilled to discover that grubs are a new taste sensation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Oral' is a noun here: a viva is a spoken university exam. A bot is the grub of a botfly.
explanation.definitionFit: A bon vivant is someone who enjoys the good life, especially fine food and drink, much as a gourmet does.

clue.text: Only one of this pair will emerge from secret meeting taking seconds

definitions.text: Only one of this pair will emerge from secret meeting taking seconds

blocks.note: surface reading: a quick clandestine rendezvous, over in moments

blocks.clueFragment: Only one of this pair will emerge
blocks.note: setter's reading: a fight to the death at dawn, attended by each side's seconds

explanation.surface: Two lovers at a brief secret tryst, only one of whom gets away.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Seconds' looks like a short time; it means the assistants who accompany each fighter at a formal affair of honour.
explanation.definitionFit: Duels were illicit, arranged in private, with each combatant attended by a second, and often only one survived.

clue.text: Looked for provision in favour of elderly

blocks.note: to be for something is to favour it
aged means old

explanation.surface: Someone sought out services supporting older people.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Provision' looks like welfare support, but it is food, as in provisions.
explanation.definitionFit: To forage is to hunt about for food or supplies, which is searching for provisions.

clue.text: Clear article on reflection’s got great depth

indicators.note: a reflection in a mirror shows things back to front

blocks.note: to clear a place of something is to rid it
an is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: A clear-cut piece of writing that turns out to be deep on reflection.
explanation.walkthrough: 'On reflection' sounds like thinking it over, but it signals the letters reading back.
explanation.definitionFit: The nadir is the lowest point, originally the spot in the sky directly beneath an observer.
